newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel weighs new Warner-Lambert diabetes drug.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel weighs new Warner-Lambert diabetes drug.

text.p: Food and Drug Administration scientists said on Wednesday that trials of the Warner-Lambert Co drug Rezulin seemed effective in treating Type II diabetes, but questioned the drug's possible side affects.
The scientists made their comments at a hearing of an FDA advisory committee that is considering whether Rezulin is safe and effective and warrants FDA approval for marketing.
The FDA is not bound by the recommendations of its committees, but usually accepts them.

Warner-Lambert officials told a hearing of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee that its trials showed the drug to be an effective and safe treatment for the type of diabetes that cannot be adequately controlled with insulin. This constitutes a population of about three million people.
The FDA scientists said they were encouraged by the efficacy of Rezulin, but that there seemed to be some safety risks involved which included the drug's effect on such internal organs as the heart.
They added that the experts on the committee would have to consider these possible risks, as well as the drug's efficacy, when they vote later today on whether to recommend FDA approval.
